transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Aurelia Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Tasha Nguyen (Infra)

Summary: Quick demo of Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and a walk through of cost breakdowns per model/route. Discussed pilot scope and security requirements.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and filtering
- Token-level cost breakdown and attribution
- Routing policies (hosted/dedicated/fallback) and autoscale behaviors
- Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering
- Next steps: send docs, run benchmarks, schedule pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, Arjun's on the call too, we'll do a quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and per-route cost breakdowns and then leave time for Qs.
[00:08] Marco: Great thanks Maya, we only have about 40 minutes so appreciate the focus, Marco here, CTO.
[00:12] Dr. Ortiz: Lena here, Head of ML, excited to see the per-route views — we want to attribute cost back to product teams.
[00:18] Arjun: Awesome, I'll share my screen, switching to the Redwood Console. Bear with me if the share lags a sec.
[00:30] Arjun: Ok, top of console you see org-level metrics, total tokens, avg latency. We'll jump into Routes which is where you can map endpoints to cost and SLAs.
[00:45] Arjun: Here's a sample route for our conversational assistant. You can see traffic over time, p50/p95 latency, model used, and token breakdown by prompt vs completion.
[00:55] Tasha: Sorry can you show me the breakdown again — where do you see per-team attribution?
[01:02] Arjun: Sure, we tag routes with metadata — service, product, owner — and then you can group by those tags. So if your front-end team owns Q/A, they get the cost bucket.
[01:12] Maya: And you can export those to CSV, or connect to billing APIs for chargeback.
[01:18] Dr. Ortiz: How granular is the token accounting? Do you show prompt vs completion tokens?
[01:23] Arjun: Yes, prompt vs completion, and we also surface prefix/KV cache hits as a separate line when enabled — that's useful because caching can change your effective cost per request.
[01:34] Marco: You said KV cache hits — is that the same as your K V cache? I just want to be sure what gets charged.
[01:40] Arjun: Yeah, sorry transcription of docs sometimes shows K V, but it's KV — key-value cache. When we cache prefixes or precomputed embeddings the console will show cache hit rate and the cost delta.
[01:50] Tasha: For our compliance needs we need to pin model versions per route and show drift over time — does the console track model version and rollout history?
[02:00] Arjun: Yes, each route record keeps a model version, rollout history, and you can do canary or A/B with automatic fallback to a compatible variant. Those events show up in the trace timeline.
[02:10] Dr. Ortiz: Nice. For cost modeling, can we see per-token cost by model? We have mixed small LLMs for simple tasks and a large one for long-form generation.
[02:20] Arjun: Absolutely. In the Cost tab you can slice by model, route, and timeframe. We also show an estimated unit cost based on our backend price and any quantization/instance differences if you're on Dedicated.
[02:34] Marco: Dedicated vs hosted — quick remind: what are the tradeoffs from the console perspective?
[02:39] Maya: Hosted gives fastest time to value and Redwood manages capacity; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput and we show separate dashboards for Dedicated capacity utilization and per-tenant billing. You can pick routing policies to favor Dedicated for high-SLA routes.
[02:54] Marco: Ok. How do I see burst usage? Like if we have a flash sale and traffic spikes?
[03:00] Arjun: We surface burst events and autoscale metrics — there's a capacity tab with current allocation, queued requests, and autoscale activity. You can set a burst policy and a fallback to a cheaper model or fallback region.
[03:12] Tasha: On security — Marco, I sent a note earlier, we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SAML/SSO. Does Redwood Console support that?
[03:22] Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and KMS integrations for Dedicated. Audit logs and per-token tracing is available; we can forward logs to your SIEM via our log forwarding integration. SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We'll share the security pack.
[03:38] Dr. Ortiz: Is there an option to run on-prem? We have some PHI use cases.
[03:43] Maya: We offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) with a private control plane and audit logging. For PHI we usually recommend Private + customer-managed KMS and retention policies.
[03:52] Marco: Good. Back to cost — can we show an example of per-route cost breakdown for a week?
[03:58] Arjun: Yep. Switching to the route: agent-assistant-prod. Here's last week's traffic. On the right you can see cost by model: 60% on gptx-large, 30% on gptx-medium, rest on cheap embedder calls. If you hover you see tokens and estimated cost.
[04:15] Arjun: We also surface recommendations — Optimize flags — like, suggest enabling a 4-bit quantized variant for gptx-medium which would reduce per-token cost by ~30% with small quality tradeoffs.
[04:27] Dr. Ortiz: Are those recommendations based on our latency SLA and observed distribution?
[04:31] Arjun: Yes, the Optimize engine looks at sequence length distribution, latency SLOs, and batch sizes, then suggests batching, cache prefixes, or quantized variants. You can preview estimated savings.
[04:43] Marco: Can we simulate cost impact if we route 20% of requests to the cheaper model?
[04:48] Arjun: There's a scenario simulator — you can input traffic mix changes and see projected monthly spend delta. I'll run a quick sim: routing 20% to medium model drops estimated spend by ~18% for this route.
[05:02] Tasha: That sim would be great to include in the spreadsheet — can you export the scenario outputs?
[05:06] Arjun: Yes, exportable CSV and as a shared dashboard link.
[05:11] Dr. Ortiz: A lot of our callbacks are long context, so latency matters. Does your cost model include GPU time for long context?
[05:18] Arjun: We model cost per token including sequence length; the console shows avg tokens per request and you can filter by long-tail requests. For Dedicated we also show GPU utilization which helps explain long-context costs.
[05:30] Marco: Any caveats about the cost numbers being estimates vs actual billing?
[05:34] Maya: The console shows estimated cost based on configured prices and model profiles. Actual invoice will match billing, but the estimates are typically within a few percent. For Dedicated we can map exact instance costs if you want line-item billing.
[05:47] [06:00-18:00] — (several minutes of screen share silence and mouse clicks)
[18:10] Arjun: Jumping back — here's per-route error analysis, you can see failed calls, trace IDs, and latencies. We integrate with Sentry and other tracing.
[18:22] Dr. Ortiz: On routing policies, we want an automatic fallback if the preferred model is overloaded — can you do model variant fallback automatically?
[18:29] Arjun: Yes — you can set policy: prefer dedicated gptx-large, fallback to hosted gptx-medium, then to a cheaper model; that fallback chain is visible in the route config and respects tokenization compatibility.
[18:40] Marco: For the pilot we'll likely want a mix: prod-critical routes on Dedicated, lower priority on Hosted. What's the onboarding look like?
[18:48] Maya: We'll start with a 30-day pilot: identify 3 routes, baseline metrics collection, run a 1-week benchmark with synthetic traffic, then tune batching/caching and produce a cost/sla report. Arjun will run the benchmarks and you'll get the per-route cost model.
[19:02] Tasha: We need the security docs before we sign anything — can you also provide penetration test results?
[19:08] Maya: We can share SOC2, pen test summary (redacted), and compliance pack. We'll send those in the follow-up.
[19:15] Dr. Ortiz: Timeline — we want to start pilot early May.
[19:20] Maya: Sounds good — we'll target week of May 4th for the benchmark.
[19:25] Marco: Anything else on routing by region? Some of our users are EU-only and need data residency.
[19:31] Arjun: You can pin routes to regions and we support region-aware routing; the console will show regional latency and regional capacity. For EU-only, you'd pick a region that stays there or run Private.
[19:44] Dr. Ortiz: One more question — how do you attribute cost for embeddings when we call them from multiple routes?
[19:50] Arjun: Embedding calls can be their own route or a shared service route; we show cross-route attribution and you can group by call origin tag to allocate embedding cost back to the originating product.
[19:59] Marco: Okay, wrapping up — recap next steps?
[20:03] Maya: Action items: Maya to send security docs and SOC2 (due 4/24), Arjun to share per-route dashboard export and cost model spreadsheet (due 4/26), Tasha to confirm VPC peering window (due 4/28). Customer will confirm pilot routes and schedule benchmark for week of 5/4.
[20:20] Dr. Ortiz: That works. One request — can you include an example of chargeback CSV with product tags so we can plug into our finance tooling?
[20:28] Arjun: Yes, we'll include a sample chargeback CSV with route tag fields.
[20:33] Marco: Thanks everyone, helpful demo.
[20:36] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up by email with the docs.
[20:40] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and minor ASR errors (KV cache transcribed as K V cache, Optimize flags sometimes shown as "optimizeings").

Referenced artifacts / links:

- Per-route cost spreadsheet (CSV) — to be shared by Arjun

End of transcript.
